Usage: drive read <session> [flags]

Print a session's newest reply, where it stands, its view, and next: where its state decides it.

Every mode prints what it read, then where the session stands, its goal as
recorded, its view and next:; a session another driver drives says so, with
no next:. A closed or gone session is read from its transcript as it ended,
with no view, since there is nothing left to act on; a gone one's next: is
the open that brings it back.

Arguments:
  <session>            The session: a label in the batch, or a block id for one outside it.

Flags:
      --prompts=N      Print the last N prompts it was told instead of its reply: what it is working
                       on and how it got there.
      --pending        Print the tool call its permission prompt waits on.
      --user           Print its newest prompt as it arrived, to see whether a step sent to it
                       landed whole.
      --screen         Print the end of its screen: a prompt's options, or whatever covers its input
                       box.
      --json           Print one JSON document instead of text.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help           Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME     Act in this batch, as drive prints its name, instead of the driver's current
                       one. It may stand anywhere on the line.
      --driver=NAME    Act in the batch this driver drives now; a chat driver's name is its
                       webhook's. It may stand anywhere on the line.

Constraints:
  At most one of --prompts, --pending, --user, --screen.

JSON:
  session, sid, goal (what it sets out to do, as recorded; left out when none is), state, account,
  input, input_text (a typed or suggested line), text (what was read), at (when it was written),
  view (left out for a closed or gone session), next, driven_by (for a session another driver's
  batch drives, its label there, the batch and the driver; it has no next), jobs (started, command)

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
